name: South Dakota

notes: Food is taxed at the full rate, 4.2% plus city taxes; only purchases with SNAP or WIC benefits are exempt. Bills to exempt food failed in 2025 (SB 213) and 2026 (HB 1281).

Alcohol bought in stores is taxed at 4.2% plus city taxes and, in 93 cities, their 1% municipal gross receipts tax, counted (each city's page says so). Excise taxes are left out: $8.50 a barrel of beer, $3.93 a gallon of spirits, wine by strength, and 2% of wholesalers' purchases of all but beer.

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at 4.2% plus city taxes, on top of excise taxes left out here: $1.53 a pack of 20 cigarettes and 35% of the wholesale price of other tobacco. Vapor products pay no excise tax.
Barber, beauty, nail and esthetician services are taxed at 4.2% plus city taxes.
Laundry and dry cleaning are taxed; coin-operated washers and dryers are exempt (their owners pay a yearly fee per machine instead), which is not taken out here.
Gasoline is exempt from the sales tax and pays a 28-cent-a-gallon motor fuel tax instead, left out here; cities may not tax motor fuel.
Repair labor is taxed, as are parts.

The state rate is 4.2% from July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2027 and returns to 4.5% on July 1, 2027 (SDCL 10-45-2); a 2026 bill to keep 4.2% (SB 195) failed in the Senate. The current 4.2% is used here.

A 1.5% state tourism tax applies to lodging, campgrounds, car and recreational rentals, visitor attractions, spectator events and recreational services all year, and from June through September to gift, souvenir and similar shops that make at least half their yearly sales then (SDCL 10-45D-2). It is not counted: no official figure gives those shops' share of sales.

Counties may adopt a sales tax of up to 0.5% for homeowner property tax relief (2026 SB 96), from January 1, 2027 at the earliest, and cities may add up to 1% for capital projects (2026 HB 1245); neither is in effect yet, and the Department of Revenue had not published any county's rate by October 30, 2026.
Car rentals of 28 days or less also pay a 4.2% motor vehicle gross receipts tax and the 1.5% tourism tax, and Sioux Falls adds a 1% lodging tax; these are outside these categories.
gaps: South Dakota counties do not levy a general sales tax; local taxes are municipal. On reservations with a tribal tax agreement the tribal tax (jurisdiction type 49, equal to the state rate) takes the place of the state tax for covered sales; it is left out, so those areas show the state rate.

Cities may add a 1% municipal gross receipts tax (SDCL 10-52A-2); 94 do (Department of Revenue, Municipal Tax Guide, July 2026). Its parts on eating places (93 cities) and on alcohol bought in stores and served (93 cities) are counted in those cities' rates; its parts on lodging and admissions are outside these categories. Each such city's page says what its tax covers.

City rates follow the Department of Revenue's own table (July 2026) where the Streamlined Sales Tax files differ: Gary 2% (the rate file has 1%), Summerset, Central City and Ward 2% (no current addresses in the boundary file) and Dupree 1% (listed under another code at 2%).
